Compute Gwet's AC2 or unweighted AC1

Source: R/api-weighted-agreement.R
gwet_ac2_table.Rd

Compute observed-score agreement across two or more raters, with a declared category universe and quadratic, linear or unweighted agreement.

Usage

gwet_ac2_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  categories,
  weights = c("quadratic", "linear", "unweighted")
)

Arguments

data

Long-format ratings with at most one row per rater and unit.

rater

Name of the rater identifier column.

unit

Names of columns jointly identifying a rated unit, such as c("Person", "Task").

score

Name of the score column. Values may be numeric, character, factor or logical, with NA for missing scores. Factors use their labels.

categories

Required distinct permitted category values, including unused categories, in their substantive order. At least two are required. They must have the same numeric/character/logical representation as scores. With linear/quadratic weights, numeric values use their actual spacing; character/logical values use equally spaced positions in this vector. Factor levels never silently determine the order. To treat numeric codes as equally spaced ranks, explicitly convert scores and categories to character. Choose spacing on substantive grounds.

weights

One of "quadratic" (default), "linear" or "unweighted". Agreement weights are 1 minus squared normalized distance, 1 minus normalized absolute distance, or the identity matrix, respectively.

Value

A plain list with table (coefficient, observed/expected agreement, status and counts), counts (category totals and unit-mean proportions), categories, weights, cases (input rows and their two inclusion flags), unit_summary, units, settings and notes. Unit indexes units. Results can be saved with base::saveRDS() without refitting on reload.

Details

Observed agreement is the equally weighted mean of within-unit weighted agreement over distinct ordered rating pairs, using only units with at least two nonmissing ratings. Category proportions are the equally weighted mean of within-unit category proportions over all units with at least one rating. Thus singletons contribute to expected agreement but not observed agreement; units with no ratings contribute to neither. This is Gwet's raw-rating convention, not Krippendorff's pairable-rating margins or Cohen's separate rater margins. Unequal rating counts do not give units greater weight.

With q declared categories, agreement matrix W and mean category proportions pi, expected agreement is sum(W) * sum(pi * (1 - pi)) / (q * (q - 1)). AC is (observed - expected)/(1 - expected). Quadratic/linear weights give AC2; identity weights give AC1. At two categories the supplied linear and quadratic weights equal identity weights, so the numerical results coincide. The complete category universe is required: adding unused categories can change expected agreement and AC. It must not be selected to improve a result.

Negative estimates are retained. No pairable units or a nonpositive chance denominator gives NA with a status. With all raters always using the same category, AC can be 1 when the declared universe has at least two categories; this does not establish discrimination, validity or reference accuracy. Unlike kappa, its chance model does not become undefined in that case.

Repeated rater-unit cells are rejected, even when scores are missing. Audits distinguish explicit missing scores from absent assignments relative to the observed rater roster. Units with no input rows are unknown. Missingness and assignment may still bias interpretation. Results are descriptive point estimates: no confidence intervals, tests, quality bands or invariance to prevalence are claimed. Different chance models answer different questions; AC2 is not an automatic replacement or correction for kappa. Dense weight storage is quadratic in the declared category count. Custom weights and circular, bipolar, radical and ratio weights are not implemented.

References

Gwet, K. L. Author implementation of AC1/AC2, gwet.ac1.raw, and linear/quadratic weights, in irrCAC. https://github.com/kgwet/irrCAC/blob/master/R/agree.coeff3.raw.r https://github.com/kgwet/irrCAC/blob/master/R/weights.gen.r

See also

pairwise_kappa_table(), krippendorff_alpha_table(), pairwise_icc_table()

Examples

data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
ac <- gwet_ac2_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", categories = 0:3)
ac$table
#>   Coefficient        AC    Status Weighting ObservedAgreement ExpectedAgreement
#> 1         AC2 0.6996106 available quadratic         0.9074074         0.6917581
#>   Raters Units PairableUnits MarginalUnits NonmissingRatings MissingScores
#> 1      3    12            12            12                34             1
#>   SingletonUnits UnratedUnits
#> 1              0            0
ac$unit_summary # Number of observed ratings and pairability for each response.
#>    Unit AssignedRows NonmissingRatings MissingScores AbsentAssignments
#> 1     1            3                 3             0                 0
#> 2     2            3                 3             0                 0
#> 3     3            3                 3             0                 0
#> 4     4            2                 2             0                 1
#> 5     5            3                 3             0                 0
#> 6     6            3                 3             0                 0
#> 7     7            3                 3             0                 0
#> 8     8            3                 3             0                 0
#> 9     9            3                 3             0                 0
#> 10   10            3                 3             0                 0
#> 11   11            3                 3             0                 0
#> 12   12            3                 2             1                 0
#>    IncludedObserved IncludedMargins ObservedAgreement
#> 1              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 2              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 3              TRUE            TRUE         0.7777778
#> 4              TRUE            TRUE         0.8888889
#> 5              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 6              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 7              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 8              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 9              TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 10             TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 11             TRUE            TRUE         0.9259259
#> 12             TRUE            TRUE         0.8888889
ac$notes # Read the panel coefficient together with its assumptions.
#> [1] "Singletons enter category proportions but not observed agreement; empty units enter neither."                 
#> [2] "Unused declared categories affect the chance model. Choose the category universe before inspecting agreement."
#> [3] "AC1/AC2, kappa and alpha use different chance models and are not interchangeable."                            
#> [4] "A high AC does not establish discrimination, reference accuracy or MFRM severity homogeneity."                
#> [5] "No confidence intervals, tests, quality bands or correction for selective missingness are supplied."
